rootCmdShort: An app that helps with fighting akrasia
rootCmdLong:
Akrasia is a word in greek that means "Incontinence", which means a lack of self-control.
This app is constructed to simply help to fight akrasía rapidly in the terminal, by adding things to do
and to keep track of these things for you.
createDailyUpdateShort: create the cron job to update daily tasks
updateDailyTodoShort: reset daily tasks for a new day and record completion history (runs via cron)
addShort: create a new task with optional description, priority, and expiration date
addExample:
akrasia add "Morning run" --daily --priority high
akrasia add "Morning run" "Do 5km at the park" --priority high
akrasia add --name "Morning run" --daily --priority high
getAllShort: returns all the todos saved in storage
todayShort: show a daily focus dashboard (overdue, due today, daily pending, expiring soon)
focusShort: show top 1-3 priority items to focus on right now
getTodoByNameShort: search for a task by name (case-insensitive, fuzzy match)
updateStatusShort: mark a task as completed and record it in history with optional notes
checkExpiredShort: show tasks that have passed their expiration date
checkExpiringShort: show tasks that have passed their expiration date
getTodoCurrentStreakShort: get the current streak of provided todo
getTodoStreakHistoryShort: get the streak history of provided todo
backfillHistoryShort: backfill missing daily task history entries
delByNameFlagDeleteYes: confirm destructive deletion of concluded tasks
deleteConcludedFlagDeleteYes: confirm destructive deletion of concluded tasks
backfillHistoryFlagDays: number of days back to backfill (default 30)
backfillHistoryFlagName: specific task name to backfill (optional, fills all daily tasks if not set)
todayFlagLimit: limit items per section (0 = no limit)
cobraHelpInfo: Use "%s [command] --help" for more information about a command.
quote1: "We suffer more often in imagination than in reality. And yet, we put off what matters to the calm, indefinite future, as if time were ours to command." - Seneca, Moral Letters to Lucilius (Letter 13).
quote2: "The present is the only time that is truly ours. To allow the mind to wander in past regret or future anxiety is the greatest theft of the self." - Marcus Aurelius, Meditations (Adapted from Book 3, 10; Book 8, 36).
quote3: "One must not think that a task is easy simply because it is not urgent. It is the non-urgent tasks that most often define the quality of a life." - Inspired by Epictetus's doctrine of prohairesis (moral character).
quote4: "The soul is dyed by the color of its thoughts. Guard, therefore, your thinking, for it becomes your action. Guard your action, for it becomes your habit." - Marcus Aurelius, Meditations (Book 5, 16).
quote5: "We must keep constant guard over our perceptions, for they are the gatekeepers of the mind." - Epictetus, Discourses (Book 4, 12).
quote6: "The mind distracted is the mind diminished. It is not a single flame but scattered embers, giving neither light nor heat." - Inspired by Plutarch's "On the Control of Anger" and the Stoic doctrine of unity of mind.
quote7: "To postpone is to choose. When you defer a good action, you have actively chosen the worse state of your soul." - Inspired by Socrates in Plato's Gorgias.
quote8: "The cause of human inaction is not that the task is large, but that the will is small. Begin, and the mind will be heated; continue, and the task will be completed." - Adapted from Democritus (Fragment 84) and the Stoic principle of "begin."
quote9: "No one errs willingly; the failure to act rightly is a failure of knowledge, not of will." - Socrates, in Plato's Protagoras
quote10: "Self-control (enkrateia) is the foundation of virtue, and the first step is to master your pleasures and appetites." - Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics
quote11: "I see and approve the better course, but I follow the worse." - Ovid, Metamorphoses
quote12: "The wise man is commanded by reason, the fool by passion, and the madman by whim." - Zeno of Citium
quote13: "How long will you wait before you demand the best for yourself?" - Epictetus, Discourses
